lesson_title: The Whole Term in One Model
hook_text: Everything you learned this term is standing on your desk. Here is how to see it.
clip_script: Look at your PAT model. The whole term is in it. Turn the crank: that is a second-class lever bent into a circle. Follow it to the gears: meshing gears turn opposite ways, and the one with more teeth turns slower and stronger. If there is a cam, it bobs; if there is a pulley, it is a wheel and axle. Now the frame. Every X-brace is two triangles so the panel cannot rack. Every upright is in compression, every string in tension, every bolt in shear, the axle in torsion. If it ever snapped, it lacked strength; bowed, stiffness; tipped, stability. Beside it, three drawings. The flat one with millimetres for the maker. The isometric, vertical and 30 degrees, to show how it fits. The coloured one to show how it looks. And behind all of it, five steps: investigate, design, make, evaluate, communicate. One model. One term. You built it, so you know it.
visual_style: A whiteboard model frame with labels popping up on each part in turn: crank, gears, braces, upright, string, axle; then three small drawings beside it; IDMEC letters across the bottom.
mood: Proud, summarising, calm before the test.
pacing: Mechanisms, structures, drawings, process: four fifteen-second sweeps across the model.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and label every part of your own model with the term's vocabulary.
